CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  Parking and Traffic Commission (PTC) Meeting
  One West Manchester Blvd., Inglewood, CA 90301
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A
  Wednesday, May 24, 2023 at 7:00 p.m.
  MAY 2023 AGENDA

COMMISSIONERS  STAFF MEMBERS
TBD, PTC Chairperson  Peter Puglese, TE, PE, City Traffic Engineer
Charles Braggs, PTC District 1  Raquel Mendez, PTC Secretary
Kip Rudd, PTC District 2  Diana Maximo, Operations Manager (LAZ Parking)
Brett C.S. Roberts, PTC District 3  William Thompson, Traffic Operations Manager (LAZ Parking)
Lois Hale, PTC District 4  Lieutenant David Salcedo, Police Department

A. Roll Call of Commissioners and Call to Order by Chairperson

B. Approval of Minutes
a. April 2023 Meeting Minutes

C. Public Comments

D. Unfinished Business
a. Mailed ballots to amend the City's Parking Permit Program on 77th Street between 8th Avenue
  and 7th Avenue on May 9, 2023. The deadline for residents to submit their ballots will be June
  9, 2023.

E. New Business (None)

F. Public Hearing
a. To amend the Citywide Parking Permit Program at 3rd Avenue from 90th Street to Manchester
  Blvd on District 7B.

G. Resolution (None)

H. Referral from City Council or City Department (None)

I. Parking and Traffic Control

J. Police Department

K. Commissioner Initiatives

L. Announcements
a. Agenda and Minutes: https://www.cityofinglewood.org/561/Parking-Traffic-Commission
b. Next Meeting date will be on June 28, 2023 at 7pm PST

M. Adjournment
MAY 2023_PTC COMMISSION MEETING AGENDA
    CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  Parking and Traffic Commission
  One West Manchester Blvd., Inglewood, CA 90301
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A
  Wednesday, May 24, 2023 at 7:00 pm
  APRIL 2023 MEETING MINUTES

A. Roll Call
a. A meeting was held at 7:05 pm in Community Room A located in the City Hall Lobby.
  Commissioner Charles Braggs, District 1, serves as interim chairperson until further notice.
b. Attendees included:
 Charles Braggs, Commissioner District 1 & Acting as Chairperson
 Kip Rudd, Commissioner District 2
 Brett C.S. Roberts, Commissioner District 3
 Lois Hale, Commissioner District 4
 William Thompson, LAZ Parking Traffic Operations Manager
 Diana Maximo, Operations Manager (LAZ Parking)
 Lieutenant G. Meeks, City of Inglewood Police Department
 Peter Puglese, City of Inglewood Principal Traffic Engineer
 Raquel Méndez, Parking and Traffic Commission Secretary

B. Approval of Minutes
a. February 2023 Meeting Minutes
 Commissioner Roberts made a motion to accept the meeting notes. Seconded by Commissioner
  Lois Hale. All Commissioners approved the meeting minutes.

C. Public Comments
a. An Oak Street Resident questioned the reason for not being on the agenda to terminate the District
  5C Residential Parking Permit. The resident inquired about having the same entitlement as the
  other Residential Parking Permit Districts. The resident asked if residents of different residential
  parking permit districts would be fined if found parked in different districts. It was responded that a
  resident who lives within the city and has the car registered with the City, no one will be fined for
  parking.

b. A 77th Street resident informed the commission that drivers are aggressively traveling on
  eastbound Century Boulevard and the resident requested more police enforcement.

c. A Holly Street resident questioned why it is not on the agenda to terminate District 5C's residential
  parking permit. The resident asked about having the same right as other districts with residential
  parking permits. The resident questioned the City's policy on the termination process and requests
  fair treatment. Before the opening of the Stadium, parking was available for residents and there
  were no problems after the opening of the Stadium. The resident questioned the parking program
  and the need to pay to park in the right-of-way. Resident demands the Parking and Commission
  to add the resident request to terminate Citywide Parking Permit Program on District 5C.

APRIL 2023_PTC COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  1 OF 4
   CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  Parking and Traffic Commission
  One West Manchester Blvd., Inglewood, CA 90301
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A
  Wednesday, May 24, 2023 at 7:00 pm
  APRIL 2023 MEETING MINUTES

d. A 77th street resident inquired about speed humps on 8th Avenue. The resident raised concerns
  about the speeding on the block. It was brought to the attention of the resident that speeding is
  an enforcement issue from the police. City staff advised that a study has been conducted and that
  speed bumps cannot be installed on 8th Avenue due to not meeting city requirements. It was
  explained that 8th Avenue is a collector street (a low to moderate capacity road that serves to
  move traffic from local streets to major roads).

e. The 97th Street and Oak Street resident asked about the dismissal of the termination permit for
  residential parking in the 5C district. Collecting the petition signatures was valuable time and
  residents believe it is unfair to not schedule the district 5C residential parking permit termination
  petition.

f. A 77th Street resident inquired about having a permit of a different parking permit district. It was
  reported that no penalty will be imposed if the resident uses their own residential parking permit
  pass in different area.

g. A 77th Street resident asked if the resident can be fined if the block is terminated from the City's
  Parking Permit Program and not registered with the program. It was responded that the resident
  will receive a citation if they do not carry a residential parking permit. The resident stated that it is
  better to apply for a parking permit rather than opt out.

h. A 95th street resident stated that forcing parking without asking the resident is not fair. The resident
  then said that the problem is not parking. It is that the resident cannot communicate with the City.

i. A resident asked how the City determines who pays to park. The resident stated that the city is
  undergoing major gentrification. Only the people who start to be negatively affected are residents.
  Living expenses have increased and no one should have to pay to park. The resident went on to
  say that if the development has parking issues, then the developers should provide it to the City.
  Residents can comply by not registering their vehicles.

j. A Holly Street resident raised the issue of segregating people by having a residential parking
  permit program. Most residents do not have the option of visiting family due to cost. The resident
  requested to bring District 5C's petition for vote and fair trial in the Parking and Traffic Commission.

k. A 95th Street resident asked about handicap parking in residential. The resident was informed
  that it is city policy that it is not allowed in residential areas. This is to prevent preferential parking
  and reduced parking spaces in the right of way.

APRIL 2023_PTC COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  2 OF 4
   CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  Parking and Traffic Commission
  One West Manchester Blvd., Inglewood, CA 90301
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A
  Wednesday, May 24, 2023 at 7:00 pm
  APRIL 2023 MEETING MINUTES

l. A 77th Street resident stated that the parking is inconvenient and does not understand the program
  where the mayor of the city has stated that raising rent is not an option for residents. The resident
  stated that residents have the right to stay in the homes that they are paying for.

D. Unfinished Business: NONE

E. New Business: NONE

F. Public Hearing
a. To amend the Citywide Parking Permit Program on 77th Street between 8th Avenue and 7th
  Avenue.
 Please visit the following link to get all the necessary information:
  https://www.cityofinglewood.org/AgendaCenter/Search/?term=&CIDs=9
 The public notice was mailed on April 10, 2023 prior to the April PTC meeting.
 On the date of the meeting, the following comments were given as to why the resident does or
  does not support the parking program:
  1. Residents rely heavily on street parking. The program is inconvenient and unreasonable.
  2. Resident would have liked to be included in the process prior to implementation of the City's
  Residential Permit Program
  3. Residents do not understand how the City bases the parking permit fee.
  4. Considering having the resident pay for parking should not have been an option, since the
  resident did not ask for any sports arenas to come to Inglewood.
  5. The Citywide Residential Permit Parking Program is illegal.
  6. The program must be aimed at visitors, not residents.
  7. All meeting attendees requested to terminate the Citywide Parking Permit Program on 77th
  Street between 8th and 7th Avenues.
 The Parking and Traffic Commission accepted the request and will proceed with the voting
  process. Commissioner Brett C.S. Roberts made a motion to accept and was seconded by
  Commissioner Charles Braggs. All four commissioners voted for the Residential Permit Parking
  District in District 5D to proceed.
 Twenty-five (25) residents attended the meeting. The sign-in sheet is attached to the minutes of
  this meeting for reference.

G. Resolution
a. The Parking and Traffic Commission signed a resolution to terminate the Citywide Parking Permit
  Program on 95th Street between 8th Avenue and 6th Avenue. A copy is attached for reference.

4  COMMISSION  RECOMMENDING  TO  THE
5  INGLEWOOD CITY COUNCIL, THE TERMINATION
6  OF THE CITYWIDE PERMIT PARKING DISTRICT 7C,
7  95TH STREET BETWEEN 8TH AVENUE AND 6TH
8  AVENUE.
9  WHEREAS, on June 16, 2020, the City Council adopted a CityWide Residential Parking
10  Permit Program (the “Program”); and
11  WHEREAS, this Program is enforced 24 hours a day / 7 days a week with 2 hour parking
12  Monday through Sunday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. (Ordinance No. 20-09); and
13  WHEREAS, the Program was adopted to more effectively and efficiently protect the
14  residential communities from non-resident vehicle intrusion; and
15  WHEREAS, on February 14, 2022, Public Works Department received a petition
16  requesting the removal of residential permit parking for District 7C, 95th Street between 8th
17  Avenue and 6th Avenue (the “District”); and
18  WHEREAS, the Public Works Department staff reviewed the petition and determined
19  that eighteen (18) valid signatures were submitted on the petition, resulting in seventy-five
20  percent (75%) of all households on the block signing the petition in favor of removing permit
21  parking restrictions; and
22  WHEREAS, on January 26, 2023, the Parking and Traffic Commission (the “Commission”)
23  held a public hearing on the issue of terminating the Residential Permit Parking Program for
24  the District and all Commissioners voted to approved the request to vote on the termination
25  on the Program; and
26  WHEREAS, on February 7, 2023, the Public Works Department, pursuant to IMC 3-76(a),
27  mailed ballots to each resident residing in the proposed permitted parking area and were
28  requested to return the ballots within thirty calendar days; and
 1  WHEREAS, on March 13, 2023, the ballots were counted. Eighteen (18) votes were cast
2  to approve the termination, while one (1) vote opposed the termination of the District; and
3  WHEREAS, a minimum of seventy-five percent (75%) of the returned ballots are required
4  to support an ordinance to the City Council for consideration and adoption of an ordinance
5  terminating the District; and
6  WHEREAS, based on the number of votes returned, ninety-five percent (95%) of the
7  households supported the termination of the District; and
8  WHEREAS, Public Works staff recommends that the Parking and Traffic Commission
9  approve and forward this resolution to the Inglewood City Council requesting that they begin
10  the process of terminating the District.
11  NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Parking and Traffic Commission of the City
12  of Inglewood, California does hereby resolve that:
13  SECTION  1.  All of the foregoing recitals are true and correct. The recitals set
14  forth above are incorporated herein and made an operative part of this resolution.
15  SECTION  2.  The Commission determined that the relevant Inglewood
16  Municipal Code was consulted and followed for terminating the City’s CityWide Permit Parking
17  Program for 7C, 95th Street between 8th Avenue and 6th Avenue.
18  SECTION  3.  The Secretary of the Commission is hereby instructed to certify a
19  copy of this resolution as evidence of the action taken by the Commission on this matter and
20  to forward a copy to the Inglewood City Council for the express purpose of recommending that
21  City Council initiate the process of terminating the CityWide Parking District 7C, 95th Street
22  between 8th Avenue and 6th Avenue.
23  SECTION  4.  If any section, subsection, clause or phrase in this Resolution or
24  the attached Exhibit, which is incorporated herein by this reference as if set for in full, is for
25  any reason held to be invalid; the validity of the remainder of the Resolution or Exhibit shall be
26  unaffected thereby.

     CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  Public Works Department
DATE:  May 24, 2023

TO:  Parking and Traffic Commission

FROM:  Peter Puglese PE, TE, City Traffic Engineer

SUBJECT: Request to Amend Residential Permit Parking District for 3rd Avenue
  from Manchester Boulevard to 90th Street

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the Parking and Traffic Commission conduct a public hearing to do
the following:
1. Receive Public Comments regarding the termination of Residential Permit Parking
  Program for 3rd Avenue from 90th Street to Manchester Boulevard within District 7B; and
2. Provide direction to the City Engineer on how to proceed

BACKGROUND:
In June 2020, the City Council adopted a Residential Permit Parking Program. The program
is enforced 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, with two-hour parking Monday through Sunday,
8 a.m. to 5 p.m. (Ordinance No. 20-09). The program was adopted to protect residential
communities more effectively and efficiently from non-resident vehicle intrusion.

On September 28, 2022, Public Works (PW) Department received a petition requesting the
removal of Residential Permit Parking for 3rd Avenue from Manchester Boulevard to 88th
Street. A second petition was filed with the Department of PW on November 24, 2022 for
3rd Avenue from 88th Street to 90th Street. The PW Department staff received and reviewed
the applications and combined them into one to be on 3rd Avenue from Manchester
Boulevard to 90th Street. Seventeen (17) valid signatures (one signature per residential
unit) were submitted on the petition, resulting in forty-two percent (42%) of all households on
the block signing the petition in favor of removing the permit parking restrictions.

On May 9, 2023, a notice was sent to the resident inviting them to the May Parking and
Traffic Commission meeting to express their views on the matter. The notice was sent to all
residents of the petition along with a buffer zone of 300 feet from the area in question.

DISCUSSION:
Residential Permit Parking Districts encourage residents to use their driveways, when
available, to park their vehicles so that those without driveways can park on the street. Public
Works staff requests the Parking and Traffic Commission provide instructions to staff on how
to proceed with the request by either:
1. Approve the request to start the voting process; or
2. Deny the request to end the processing of the petition.

 Inglewood  California
  Inglewood Parking and Traffic Commission
  (Comisión de Estacionamiento y Tráfico de la Ciudad de Inglewood)

  AVISO DE AUDIENCIA PÚBLICA
  Petición de Eliminación del Permiso de
  Estacionamiento en la Zona Residencial
Se ha presentado una petición al Departamento de Obras Públicas de Inglewood solicitando la cancelación
del Permiso de Estacionamiento Residencial dentro del Distrito 7B en 3rd Avenue entre 90th Street y
Manchester Blvd. De acuerdo con las Secciones 3-75 a 3-79 del Código Municipal de Inglewood, este
asunto se presentará a la Comisión de Estacionamiento y Tráfico de Inglewood a la hora y lugar
especificados:

  Miércoles 24 de Mayo de 2023 a las 7:00p.m.
  En la Sala Comunitaria A en el Primer Piso
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

Este aviso se envía por correo a todas las direcciones que se encuentran al frente de la calle en cuestión.
Cualquier persona interesada puede asistir a esta reunión y hablar sobre este tema.

  Propósito de la Audiencia Pública
El propósito de esta audiencia pública es brindar a todos los residentes de las áreas específicas
enumeradas anteriormente la oportunidad de expresar su opinión sobre el tema. El propósito del Programa
de Permisos de Estacionamiento Residencial es garantizar la disponibilidad para los residentes de algunos
espacios de estacionamiento en la calle (bordillo) dentro de un vecindario donde los clientes y/o empleados
de una instalación comercial o industrial cercana utilizan todos los espacios de estacionamiento disponibles
en la calle.

La Comisión de Tráfico y Estacionamiento de Inglewood, por lo tanto, considerará si la disponibilidad de
estacionamiento en la calle se ve gravemente afectada de esta manera y si se justificaría la terminación de
un Permiso de Estacionamiento Residencial dentro del Distrito 7B en 3rd Avenue entre 90th Street y
Manchester Blvd. Si se determina que está justificado, las boletas se enviarán por correo a cada hogar
dentro del distrito de estacionamiento propuesto. Se requiere una aprobación del setenta y cinco por ciento
(75 %) para eliminar un distrito de estacionamiento con permiso residencial.

Si se elimina un Distrito de Estacionamiento con Permiso Residencial, no se restringirá el estacionamiento
en las calles públicas a todos los residentes y visitantes de este vecindario en ningún momento; incluso
durante los eventos especiales. Si tiene alguna pregunta sobre este asunto o desea expresar una opinión
pero no puede asistir a la audiencia pública, comuníquese con el Departamento de Obras Públicas de
Inglewood al (310) 412-5333.
 Inglewood  California
  Inglewood Parking and Traffic Commission
  NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING
  Petition for Elimination of Permit Parking in
  Residential Neighborhood
A petition has been submitted to the Inglewood Public Works Department requesting the termination of
Residential Permit Parking within District 7B at 3rd Avenue from 90th Street to Manchester Blvd. Per
Sections 3-75 to 3-79 of the Inglewood Municipal Code, this matter will be presented to the Inglewood
Parking and Traffic Commission at the time and place specified:

  Wednesday May 24, 2023 at 7:00 p.m.
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

This notice is being mailed to all addresses fronting the subject street. Any interested person may attend
this meeting and speak on this matter.

  Purpose of Public Hearing
The purpose of this public hearing is to give all residents of the specific areas listed above an opportunity
to state their opinion of the subject matter.

The purpose of the Residential Permit Parking Program is to assure the availability to residents of some on-
street (curbside) parking spaces within a neighborhood where the patrons and/or employees of a nearby
commercial or industrial facility are otherwise using all available on-street parking spaces.

The Inglewood Parking and Traffic Commission will therefore be considering if the availability of on-street
parking is severely impacted in this manner and if the termination of a Residential Permit Parking within
District 7B at 3rd Avenue from 90th Street to Manchester Blvd would be warranted. If it is determined to be
warranted, ballots will be mailed to each household within the proposed parking district. A seventy-five
percent (75 %), approval is required to eliminate a Residential Permit Parking District.

If a Residential Permit Parking District is eliminated, all residents and visitors in this neighborhood will not
be restricted from parking on the public streets at any time; including during special events. If you have any
questions regarding this matter, or wish to express an opinion but are unable to attend the public hearing,
please contact the Inglewood Public Works Department at (310) 412-5333.
